newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX falls on political, econ uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX falls on political, econ uncertainty.

text.p: Continued political and economic uncertainty helped push Slovak share prices down on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with brokers expecting more stagnation in the coming days.
The SAX index fell 3.18 points to 194.51.

Only 487 shares traded on the BSE listed floor, 377 of which were steel maker VSZ, after weekend referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections were declared invalid, amid cries of foul from both opposition and government members, and the resignation of Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik.
"The political uncertainty which resulted from the chaos over failed weekend referendum has clearly contributed to this situation," said Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt.
Adding to the instability was increased pressure on the Slovak crown following the fall of the Czech crown to a wave speculation, and poor trade figures for April.
"It's meaningless to talk about the capital market unless it is clear what will happen to the currency," Krutil said.

"The central bank must give at least some signal," he said adding high interest rates have paralyzed investors and choked liquidity. "I don't see any improvement without all these unknowns being solved," he added.
Overall volume increased to 463,565 shares, from 452,445 shares traded on Monday, while turnover, boosted by mainly by direct and block deals, rose to 118.53 million crowns, from 81.45 million.
